415:     fn run_program(

423:         #[cfg(not(unix))]
424:         let arg0 = prog.clone();
425:         let args = &opts.program[1..];
426: 
427:         /*
428:          * On Unix-like systems Command::status either ends up calling either fork or posix_spawnp
429:          * (which ends up calling clone). Keep using the current process would be ideal, but the
430:          * standard library contains many checks and fail-safes to ensure the process ends up being
431:          * created. This is much simpler than dealing with the hassles of calling execvp directly.
432:          */
433:         let mut cmd = process::Command::new(&*prog);
434:         cmd.args(args);
435: 
436:         if let Some(_argv0) = opts.argv0 {
437:             #[cfg(unix)]
438:             {
439:                 cmd.arg0(_argv0);
440:                 arg0 = Cow::Borrowed(_argv0);
441:                 if do_debug_printing {
442:                     eprintln!("argv0:     {}", arg0.quote());
443:                 }
444:             }
445: 
446:             #[cfg(not(unix))]
447:             return Err(USimpleError::new(
448:                 2,
449:                 "--argv0 is currently not supported on this platform",
450:             ));
451:         }
452: 
453:         if do_debug_printing {
454:             eprintln!("executing: {}", prog.maybe_quote());
455:             let arg_prefix = "   arg";
456:             eprintln!("{}[{}]= {}", arg_prefix, 0, arg0.quote());
457:             for (i, arg) in args.iter().enumerate() {
458:                 eprintln!("{}[{}]= {}", arg_prefix, i + 1, arg.quote());
459:             }
460:         }
461: 
462:         match cmd.status() {
463:             Ok(exit) if !exit.success() => {
464:                 #[cfg(unix)]
465:                 if let Some(exit_code) = exit.code() {
466:                     return Err(exit_code.into());
467:                 } else {
468:                     // `exit.code()` returns `None` on Unix when the process is terminated by a signal.
469:                     // See std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt for more information. This prints out
470:                     // the interrupted process and the signal it received.
471:                     let signal_code = exit.signal().unwrap();
472:                     let signal = Signal::try_from(signal_code).unwrap();

474:                     // We have to disable any handler that's installed by default.
475:                     // This ensures that we exit on this signal.

479:                     // just defaulting to default behavior and not installing a function. Hence, the call
480:                     // is safe.
481:                     let _ = unsafe {
482:                         sigaction(
483:                             signal,
484:                             &SigAction::new(SigHandler::SigDfl, SaFlags::empty(), SigSet::all()),
485:                         )
486:                     };
487: 
488:                     let _ = raise(signal);
489:                 }
490:                 return Err(exit.code().unwrap().into());
491:             }
492:             Err(ref err)
493:                 if (err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound)
494:                     || (err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput) =>
